text:
Alex: FYI regen-check flagged a minor bump on clients/js even though only generated docs changed. Anyone seen this pattern?
Priya: Yep, examples in the OpenAPI moved order. typegen treats that as changed comment blocks.
Sam: CI excerpt: ```Error: New typegen output differs
diff --git a/clients/js/src/index.ts b/clients/js/src/index.ts
@@ -12,6 +12,8 @@
+  // example: signup flow (order changed)
   export function createClient() {}
```
ci-bot: Build 848101 failed at regen-check (typegen-regressions).
Maya: We have an open spec normalizer but it runs as a linter job, not during publishflow. If CI's publishflow runs typegen before lint, we get nondeterministic diffs.
Jordan: Two fixes: run normalization step prior to typegen in publishflow, and make typegen detect "examples-only" diffs and mark them docs.
Priya: Local repro: run `node scripts/normalize-openapi.js` then `yarn typegen` -> diff disappears. I'll attach a small script to CI.
devex-bot: Created issue #7732: "publishflow: normalize OpenAPI before typegen to avoid example-order regen diffs" assigned to @Sam and @Priya.
Alex: Plan: 1) Sam hotfixes CI step to normalize spec before typegen, 2) Priya adds typegen guard to ignore example-only changes, 3) Maya will monitor any accidental publishes and rollback if needed.
Sam: Opening hotfix PR now, will include unit test that shuffles examples to assert no diff. ETA ~2h.
Priya: Will scope typegen change carefully so we don't mask real API surface changes.
Maya: Also watch sample-app CI for auth/retry flakiness after publish; last time a minor bumped sample tests hit a timing-sensitive retry test. Report any flakes here.
Alex: Thanks all. If publish needs rollback ping @dev-oncall. :thumbsup:
